title: བསྟན་འགྱུར། སྡེ་དགེ། ཚད་མ། མེ (Derge Tengyur, vol. 185)
shelf_note: Derge Tengyur Pramāṇa (Tshad ma) section commentary volume 'me' (vol. 185), treating classical Indian Buddhist epistemological debates on perception and the causes of doubt.

ocr_errors.problem: Systematic misreading of 'sdong dum' (post/stump, sthāṇu) as 'sdong gru' across lines 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 7
Misread ''greng ba' (upright / erect) as ''brang ba' (following / pursuing), corrupting the concluding epistemological definition

tr_errors_A.english: Because it is not the case, memory is the cause of doubt
tr_errors_A.problem: Clumsy rendering of 'ma yin pas' as an independent clause ('Because it is not the case') rather than connecting to non-perception as the condition for memory
Mistranslated rhetorical question particle 'ji ltar' ('How [could both be seen]?') as comparative 'Just as'

tr_errors_B.english: to the objection that what appears in common...
tr_errors_B.problem: Sentence starts with lowercase 'to', missing initial capitalization

tr_errors_B.english: at one time, neither is seen
tr_errors_B.problem: Mistranslated 'gnyis ka mthong ba med do' ('both are not seen [together]') as 'neither is seen'

tr_errors_B.english: Therefore, does one not entertain doubt?
tr_errors_B.problem: Reversed the opponent's negative assertion ('therefore doubt does not arise') into a question asking if doubt is entertained

tr_errors_B.english: Cognition is determined to follow this.
tr_errors_B.problem: Blindly translated the OCR error ''brang ba' ('following') instead of the woodblock text ''greng ba' ('upright'), completely obscuring the perceptual determination of uprightness in the classic post/person doubt debate

pages.prefer_reason: Translation A correctly reads the image's key epistemological predicate 'upright' (འགྲེང་བ་) where B translates an OCR error as 'follow this', and A properly identifies the misread 'sdong gru' as a post or tree trunk.

book_verdict: Authentic Derge Tengyur woodblock print folio on Buddhist epistemology; the OCR contains systematic misreadings ('sdong dum' -> 'sdong gru' and ''greng ba' -> ''brang ba') which Translation A successfully overcomes while Translation B propagates as serious translation errors.
